key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained with masked objectives and contrastive learning yields rich small-molecule natural product representations that improve taxonomy classification, genome mining and virtual screening performance.
problem_solved: Current models struggle to capture scaffold-level structure and semantic relationships in diverse natural products, limiting accuracy and transferability across tasks like taxonomic labeling, biosynthetic gene cluster discovery and ligand screening.
method: Scaffold-aware representation: encode molecules with explicit scaffold information to preserve core structural motifs essential to natural products.
Masked reconstruction objectives: pretrain the model to recover masked substructures and chemical features to learn contextual chemical semantics.

Contrastive learning: align augmented views of the same molecule and separate different molecules in embedding space to sharpen taxonomy- and activity-relevant distinctions; fine-tune on downstream tasks (taxonomy classification, genome mining, virtual screening).
impact: Delivers a general-purpose pretrained model tailored to natural products that improves downstream prediction and retrieval tasks, accelerating computational natural product discovery and reducing experimental screening burden for AI/ML practitioners in cheminformatics and drug discovery.

paper_title: Pretraining a foundation model for small-molecule natural products
paper_authors: Yuheng Ding, Bo Qiang, Shaoning Li, Yiran Zhou, Jie Yu
